_what: NOS is two unrelated terms in the same market, and this catalogue uses one of them as a technical state. Written 2026-11-24 after Nagra's HD DAC X page used the other one.
_ours: NOS = non-oversampling. A converter run with no interpolation filter ahead of it. It matters because `correctable` turns on it: the field's own definition says corrections exist in practice « only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM ». So NOS is a precondition for a per-device correction profile, which makes it one of the most consequential states a record can hold.
_theirs: NOS = New Old Stock. Unused valves from discontinued production, prized and advertised as such. Nagra: « two NOS military JAN5963 tubes (one per channel) ». Nothing to do with oversampling; it is a statement about where the parts came from.
_the_failure_it_would_cause: A text search for NOS across harvested sources would mark the HD DAC X non-oversampling. That device is an FPGA machine whose page says « Every input signal is converted into DSD 256 format » - resampling everything, the exact opposite of non-oversampling - and marking it NOS would make it eligible for a correction profile it must never receive. The error is silent: nothing downstream would contradict it.
_how_to_tell_them_apart: New Old Stock appears next to a valve type number (JAN5963, 6922, 101D), in a sentence about the output or power stage. Non-oversampling appears next to a filter, a sample rate, a ladder or the word oversampling itself. If the sentence is about a part's PROVENANCE it is stock; if it is about the SIGNAL PATH it is the filter. When a page says only « NOS » with no context, it settles nothing and the field stays absent.
_where_this_bites_hardest: At the top of the market, where valves are a selling point: Nagra, LampizatOr, APL HiFi, Aries Cerat and others advertise NOS valves, and several of those same makers also build genuinely non-oversampling converters. A record can honestly carry both meanings at once, in different fields, and a guard that greps for the three letters cannot.
